title: Chatbot to improve learning punctuation in Spanish and to enhance open and flexible learning environments
venue: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether a chatbot can improve students’ punctuation performance in Spanish compared with a more traditional practice-based approach. The authors focus on punctuation as a foundational writing skill and ask whether conversational, mobile, and feedback-rich chatbot activities can support better learning than paper-based exercises.

The intervention was implemented in the access course of the National University of Distance Education (UNED) in Spain over two academic years. Students first received the same face-to-face instruction in punctuation, then were split into a control group and an experimental group. The control group completed a PDF dossier of punctuation exercises with self-evaluation, while the experimental group practiced with two chatbots built on the Collect.chat platform. Neither group received tutorial support during the practice period. Outcomes were measured with pretest and posttest punctuation exams, and the experimental group also provided forum feedback that was analyzed textually.

Results showed that both groups started at similar levels, but the chatbot group improved significantly more on the final punctuation test. Gains were especially noted for periods, colons, and commas. Students also reported positive perceptions of the chatbot, especially its support, interactivity, feedback, mobility, and ease of use. The authors conclude that chatbots can be a useful tool for language learning, particularly for practice-oriented skills that benefit from repeated feedback and flexible access.

identified_tools.name: Collect.chat
identified_tools.description: A drag-and-drop chatbot builder platform for creating conversational bots without programming knowledge.
identified_tools.use_case: Used to design and deliver two punctuation chatbots for Spanish-language practice in a blended learning university access course.

findings.finding_summary: Students in the experimental group who practiced with the chatbot outperformed the control group on the final punctuation test. The paper reports posttest means of 32.1346 for the experimental group and 28.4706 for the control group, with a significant difference (sig. 0.000).

quality_tier_rationale: This is a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest study with a control group and a clearly described comparison condition, but it is not randomized and uses convenience sampling. The paper reports inferential statistics and a defined intervention, supporting moderate evidentiary strength.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported posttest difference is statistically significant and the improvement is substantial in magnitude for the punctuation outcome, with the experimental group mean exceeding the control group by over four points. The paper also reports positive category-level effects for several punctuation marks, indicating meaningful impact on literacy performance.
